title: Tracing a single call and a chain of calls

videos.script: This course runs a language model on your own computer. The lesson opens by installing it, with Ollama, and building the shop the course watches. {{setup}} A customer asks Marginalia's assistant who pays the postage on a return. The answer comes back in three seconds, with a citation. It is wrong, and nothing on the screen says so. {{answer}} This lesson puts a record behind every answer. One span around a model call: what was asked for, what answered, how many tokens, how long. {{span}} Then the whole chain. The question is embedded, the documents are searched, the model writes, the citations are checked. Each step is a span, nested under one root. {{tree}} Read the tree and the time is easy to place. Nearly all of it is the model. {{time}} Read the attributes and the wrong answer points at its cause. The search found the right paragraph, the one that says returns are free. The model read it, and said the opposite. {{why}} A library can write these spans for you. Look at what it keeps when it does. {{library}} And every trace has an id, which is what feedback, scores and support tickets will join to. {{id}} What a trace cannot tell you is whether the answer was right. That takes the second half of the course. {{end}}
